fixes.prompt:
Kane CLI (a real-browser test agent) just found cross-user data leaks in this app.

The owner (alice) created a private note at http://localhost:3000/notes/107 containing the canary "CANARY-ebda5238".
Other people could read it:
- intruder-page: as intruder, Kane opened http://localhost:3000/notes/107 and saw the owner's secret "CANARY-ebda5238". Kane said: "Bob can open note 107 and see the protected CANARY text when it should not be visible.". Screenshot: C:\Users\Toleexxzy\OneDrive\Documents\coding projects\zelkaro\zelkaro-report\screenshots\round-1-2-intruder-page.jpg
- intruder-api: as intruder, Kane opened http://localhost:3000/api/notes/107 and saw the owner's secret "CANARY-ebda5238". Kane said: "While signed in as bob, the page exposed the canary text from note 107, which belongs to alice.". Screenshot: C:\Users\Toleexxzy\OneDrive\Documents\coding projects\zelkaro\zelkaro-report\screenshots\round-1-3-intruder-api.jpg
- anonymous-page: as anonymous, Kane opened http://localhost:3000/notes/107 and saw the owner's secret "CANARY-ebda5238". Kane said: "The page shows the protected CANARY text even though the visitor did not log in.". Screenshot: C:\Users\Toleexxzy\OneDrive\Documents\coding projects\zelkaro\zelkaro-report\screenshots\round-1-4-anonymous-page.jpg
- anonymous-api: as anonymous, Kane opened http://localhost:3000/api/notes/107 and saw the owner's secret "CANARY-ebda5238". Kane said: "The page exposes the canary text without logging in, so the required absence check correctly failed.". Screenshot: C:\Users\Toleexxzy\OneDrive\Documents\coding projects\zelkaro\zelkaro-report\screenshots\round-1-5-anonymous-api.jpg

Fix the access control so a note can only be read by its owner, on every route listed above (pages and API).
Rules:
- The owner must still be able to read their own note. Kane re-checks this, so denying everyone fails.
- Fix the root cause in the authorization logic. Do not hide content with CSS or rename routes.
- Do not edit zelkaro.config.json, the canary, or anything under zelkaro-report/.
- Hint from the project: Authorization for notes lives in demo/policies.js.

When done, reply with two sentences: what was wrong and what you changed.
fixes.reply: The leak came from `canReadNote()` in `demo/policies.js`: it returned `true` for everyone, so Bob and logged-out visitors could read Alice's note on both `/notes/:id` and `/api/notes/:id`, since both routes use that one check. I changed it to return true only when a user is signed in and their `user.id` matches the note's `owner`, which keeps Alice's access and denies everyone else — I haven't re-run Kane yet, but the server reloads `policies.js` on each request, so a re-scan should pick up the fix with no restart.
